text: In the early hours of the morning the city had not yet woken up. The street lamps had gone out, and short queues were beginning to form in front of the bakeries. As the fishermen returned to the harbour, seagulls circled above the boats. After breakfast we went to the market; we bought tomatoes, cucumbers and fresh bread. Towards noon the air grew warm, and children were playing ball in the park. When evening came the lights of the bridge came on and the ferries set off towards the opposite shore. An old man sat on a bench reading a newspaper; he greeted the passers-by with a smile. Towards midnight the rain began and the streets emptied all at once. The next morning everything was clean and bright, as if it had been washed.
